subject: Audit extractability, snapshot cadence & delivery timelines (RFP follow-up)
messages:

Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@stonebridge.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP question: ad-hoc snapshot turnaround & export formats

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP response packet — quick clarification from our side on two items before we finalize the scoring: 

1) For ad-hoc forensic snapshots (legal hold / incident response), what is your typical turnaround SLA for delivery of a full audit bundle (logs + KV snapshots + metadata)? Please separate for hosted vs. private deployments.

2) What export formats do you support for audit bundles (e.g., ndjson, parquet, protobuf) and do you include tamper-evidence hashes and chain-of-custody manifests?

We need answers by COB next Monday to keep the procurement timeline.

Appreciate it —
Samira Khan
Security & Resilience
Stonebridge Capital
samira.khan@stonebridge.com

Attachments: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@stonebridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: ad-hoc snapshot turnaround & export formats

Samira —

Thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers up front, and I've looped in Karthik and Naomi for the technical and legal specifics. Please see the short bullets below; we can provide a short package/deliverable template if you want to share a preferred playbook.

- Turnaround SLA (hosted): standard ad-hoc evidence bundles are delivered within 72 hours for high-priority requests; expedited 24-hour delivery available with dedicated commitment (Dedicated tier).
- Turnaround SLA (private/VPC or on-prem): typical ship time is 5 business days (allowing for customer-run access approvals); we offer an expedited channel (1–3 business days) when we have pre-approved connectors and a signed evidence-handoff SOP.
- Export formats: NDJSON (event stream), Parquet (columnar), and compressed tarballs containing JSON+manifest. We also support CSV extracts for sampled slices.
- Tamper-evidence: yes — each bundle contains SHA-256 digests for constituent files and a signed manifest (PKS-based) which can be verified against the evidence package.

Karthik / Naomi — can you confirm the delivery packaging details and whether we can attach a sample manifest + draft playbook?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: none
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: ad-hoc snapshot turnaround & export formats

Marissa / Samira —

Confirming the packaging and adding technical caveats:

- Bundle contents: (1) event stream (ndjson) with per-event timestamps and source routing, (2) KV snapshots exported as JSON/ndjson with sequence numbers, (3) model-serving metadata (model id, version, kernel profile), (4) system-level telemetry (host traces) where permitted, (5) signed manifest (manifest.json) with per-file SHA-256 and a top-level signed envelope.
- Integrity: we sign manifests using our HSM-backed key (customer-verifiable public key can be supplied). Chain-of-custody fields include requested_by, exported_by, export_job_id, and export_timestamp.
- Export size & delivery: typical small-to-medium customer bundle (30–150GB) is staged to S3 and a presigned URL is provided; for very large exports we arrange a physical transfer or multipart presigned upload.
- Retention windows: audit logs retained 90 days by default on hosted, with tiered options (365/730/custom) — retention policies are configurable per account and reflected in the manifest.
- Snapshot cadence: Forensic snapshots can be taken on-demand; we can also schedule periodic snapshots (daily/weekly/monthly). Note: KV snapshot granularity depends on model cache eviction windows; we include a coverage note in the manifest.

I've attached the current export playbook and a sample SLA table for turnaround/cost assumptions.

--Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: export-playbook-v1.pdf (17MB), snapshot-sla-table.xlsx (43KB)
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@stonebridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@stonebridge.com>, procurement@stonebridge.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: ad-hoc snapshot turnaround & export formats

Marissa / Karthik —

This is very helpful — thanks. A couple of follow-ups: 

- For hosted exports, can you confirm whether the manifest includes a stable mapping from log UUID -> canonical timestamp (i.e., is there any possibility of reordering during export)? We need to be able to reconstruct event order for e-discovery.
- For private deployments, does the expedited 1–3 day channel require a dedicated Redwood operator to be provisioned on the customer network (we'd prefer minimizing cross-network operator requirements).
- Can you provide an example manifest (sanitized) and a sample presigned URL workflow so our infra team can validate tooling compatibility?

If you can get the sample manifest and a short runbook to us by EOD Wednesday we'll be able to keep this locked to the next procurement window.

Best,
Samira
